solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Correct Option Analysis:**

The correct option is:

**Option 3:** A - S, B - R, C - Q, D - P

This option correctly matches the designations of the trimmed sizes of sheets with their respective lengths and widths. Let’s analyze each designation and its corresponding trimmed size:

 
• **A0 - S (841 × 1189 mm):** A0 is the largest size in the A series of paper sizes, and its trimmed dimensions are 841 mm × 1189 mm. This is the standard size for A0, as defined by ISO 216.
 
• **A1 - R (594 × 841 mm):** The A1 paper size is half the area of A0 and its dimensions are 594 mm × 841 mm. This size is also in accordance with ISO 216 standards.
 
• **A2 - Q (420 × 594 mm):** A2 is half the area of A1 and has dimensions of 420 mm × 594 mm. The trimmed size is correct as per the ISO standard.
 
• **A3 - P (297 × 420 mm):** A3 is half the area of A2 and its dimensions are 297 mm × 420 mm. This size matches the standard definition for A3 paper size.

**Analysis of Other Options:**

To further understand the correctness of Option 3, let’s evaluate the other options:

**Option 1:** A - P, B - R, C - Q, D - S

In this option:

 
• A0 is incorrectly matched with P (297 × 420 mm). A0 is the largest size, and its correct dimensions are 841 × 1189 mm.
 
• A1 is correctly matched with R (594 × 841 mm).
 
• A2 is correctly matched with Q (420 × 594 mm).
 
• A3 is incorrectly matched with S (841 × 1189 mm). A3 is smaller than A2 and its correct dimensions are 297 × 420 mm.

Hence, Option 1 is incorrect.

**Option 2:** A - S, B - R, C - P, D - Q

In this option:

 
• A0 is correctly matched with S (841 × 1189 mm).
 
• A1 is correctly matched with R (594 × 841 mm).
 
• A2 is incorrectly matched with P (297 × 420 mm). A2 is larger than A3 and its correct dimensions are 420 × 594 mm.
 
• A3 is incorrectly matched with Q (420 × 594 mm). A3 is smaller than A2 and its correct dimensions are 297 × 420 mm.

Therefore, Option 2 is incorrect.
